column1: # tests/expected/shared_wall_push.tsv — who keeps a shared corner: the push-apart at the landing frame, per engine
# (tests/audit_shared_wall_push.sh; tests/lua/read_tap.lua, non-debug). Evidence class: in-emulator (MAME, pristine
# vsavj, native vsav2 and the WIDE build m3b_merged28; frames >= 2300). Frozen 14z-184 (GitHub #179, ruled the host
# engine's behaviour) with FREEZE=1, its rule-checker run named in the commit. A push row that changes PC or fighter,
# a new non-zero +0x148 writer on vsavj or ours, or a legacy first split that moves EARLIER than the landing is a
# finding; a landing frame that moves means the rig moved — re-derive before re-freezing.
# Columns: part, leg, kind (push | flag148-set | end | ids | first-split), frames, value
#   push: every x write by the push-apart routine in the window, <frame>:<pc>:<fighter>:<x hex>
#   flag148-set: every PC storing a non-zero byte to either fighter's +0x148; end: both x at that frame;
#   ids: the last pre-match id byte per fighter (the picks are real, never poked); first-split: the legacy legs'
# Frame numbers are read_tap.lua's WRITE labels: a write labelled N is the state replay.lua and field_trace.lua
# sample as frame N+1 (measured 14z-184, every unpoked frame of all four legs; the gate re-proves it each run).
